thread.title: Stock futures point lower ahead of jobs report

author: Ken Martin
title: Stock futures point lower ahead of jobs report
text:
Stocks erase early losses from jobs report By Leia Klingel Published May 04, 2018 Stocks FOXBusiness video These two things together can bring down the stock market
“The Bubba Show” host Todd Horwitz says if the 10-year treasury yield goes over 3%, while the dollar remains strong, it will bring down the markets. All major share indexes climbed Friday, with consumer and technology stocks, especially Apple, pulling up other sectors. Friday’s rally was lifting shares on the Nasdaq Composite out of correction territory for the week. Apple shares climbed after Warren Buffett revealed that Berkshire Hathaway bought 75 million more Apple shares last quarter. Apple entered its second correction this year on April 24 after falling more than 10% below the March 12 record close of $181.72. To finish out of correction, Apple needs to close above $178.55. Investors found the April jobs report, released before the markets opened, a mixed bag. There were 164,000 jobs created in April, less than the 192,000 expected but more than the previous month. The unemployment rate fell to 3.9%, according to the Labor Department. Last month’s job creation was above the revised 135,000 March reading. April’s 3.9% unemployment is the lowest since 2000, and wage growth remained unchanged, at 2.6% over the past 12 months. A positive of the jobs report, according to JJ Kinahan, is with monthly job creation numbers dropping below their 200,000 peaks, is a lower likelihood of the economy overheating. “I don’t see the economy overheating in a hurry,” he said. Kinahan added that, six months ago, the Federal Reserve had concerns that when inflation came, it would come at an exponential fashion.
